title: Overcoming a Learning Bottleneck in Impartial Games: A Circuit Complexity Approach
abstract: arXiv:2411.06403v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Why can neural networks struggle to learn optimal play in a game with a simple, efficient solution algorithm? Motivated by empirical difficulties with parity in impartial games, we use NIM to study a representational bottleneck and three ways around it. We show that a restricted model of shallow, fixed-scale quantised networks lies in $\mathrm{AC}^0$, a circuit class unable to compute parity on arbitrarily large inputs. This prevents optimal single-position play across all board sizes within the model. The obstruction also guides architectural design: two-frame inputs allow restoration from a known zero-nim-sum position; complementary rollout policies reveal the missing invariant; and persistent recurrence accumulates it row by row. Each route retains shallow network components while supplying additional information or processing time. Supervised experiments illustrate the benefits of two-frame restoration and multiple rollout heads;

translated_title: 克服公平组合游戏中的学习瓶颈：一种电路复杂度方法
translated_abstract: 为什么神经网络在一个拥有简单高效求解算法的游戏中难以学习最优策略？受公平组合游戏中奇偶性问题的经验性困难启发，我们使用NIM（尼姆游戏）来研究一个表征瓶颈及绕过它的三种方法。我们证明了一个受限的浅层、固定规模量化网络模型属于AC⁰电路类，而该电路类无法在任意大的输入上计算奇偶性。这使得该模型无法在所有棋盘规模上实现最优的单位置决策。这一障碍同时也指导了架构设计：双帧输入允许从已知的零尼姆和位置进行恢复；互补的展开策略能够揭示缺失的不变量；而持续递归则可以逐行累积该不变量。每条路径都保留了浅层网络组件，同时提供额外的信息或处理时间。监督学习实验展示了双帧恢复机制和多个展开头的优势。
tldr: 本文利用电路复杂度理论证明了浅层固定规模量化网络属于无法计算奇偶性的AC⁰电路类，从而解释了神经网络学习NIM游戏最优策略的表征瓶颈，并提出双帧输入、互补展开策略和持续递归三种克服该瓶颈的架构设计方案。
en_tdlr: Using circuit complexity, this paper proves that shallow fixed-scale quantized networks lie in AC⁰—a class unable to compute parity—explaining why neural networks struggle to learn optimal NIM play, and proposes three architectural solutions: two-frame inputs, complementary rollout policies, and persistent recurrence.
